title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 13
paragraphs: These, then, had such a night as I have described; and meanwhile those of them assigned to sail around Euboea experienced that very same night, but it raged against them much more fiercely, inasmuch as it fell upon them while they were making their course in the open sea. And the end of it was disastrous for them: for when the storm and the rain came on together as they sailed, off the “Hollows” of Euboea, they were driven by the wind not knowing which way they were being carried, and were cast upon the rocks. All this was being brought about by God so that the Persian force might be made more evenly matched with the Greek, and not greatly outnumber it.
